Lee’s Summit Remodeling & Design

Life is better in a space you love.

At Haven Reno KC, we are a woman-owned home remodeling and design company based in Lee's Summit, Missouri. We specialize in bathroom remodeling, kitchen remodeling, and basement finishing. 

With our skilled team of project managers, designers and contractors, you can rest easy knowing your renovation will be taken care of from start to finish. Send us a message or give us a call for a free quote! We'd love to help with your project. 

GET FREE ESTIMATE
What We Offer

If you’re looking for a home transformation, we’ve got you covered. We offer interior design and remodeling for any space inside your home. We do basements, kitchens, bathrooms, laundry rooms, bedrooms, offices, playrooms and more. Check out some of our most recent work.

The planning & design was fun instead of overwhelming, and the vision we had for our home was brought to life in a timely, professional manner. The quality of their work is evident, and they respected our home while doing it. We are already considering other projects that they can help us with!”

Meet The Owners

Your Renovation Team

Lorna McCartney

PROJECT MANAGER + DESIGNER

Lorna has been passionate about design since renovating her own first home in 2006. 

Once a dedicated nurse practitioner, Lorna decided to embark on a new chapter in her life to follow her heart's calling. Her transition from the medical field to renovation and design was driven by a desire to create spaces that inspire and uplift the human spirit. 

Lorna's design philosophy is rooted in her love of clean, efficient spaces coupled with serene colorways and laid-back vibes of the coastline. As a mother of two, she understands the importance of creating spaces that are not only beautiful but functional for families. She prides herself in her attention to detail and commitment to quality and believes that every space should reflect a homeowner’s personality and lifestyle. 

Mel Kelly

GENERAL CONTRACTOR + DESIGNER

Mel is a contemporary artist turned interior designer & General Contractor here in the Kansas City area. Mel’s passion for design burst into life back in 2011 as she and her husband remodeled their first home. Through that process she began creating custom artwork and eventually selling art for interiors from Maui to NYC.

She strengthened her design portfolio through running her own home decor business (Not Boring Home) from 2019-2022. Her work for Not Boring Home landed her shop in The World of Interiors and House & Garden Magazine. 

Now she brings that passion for art and contemporary design to your home. Mel’s personal mission is to help turn your space into a haven where you can be yourself and live your best life.

We’re Featured on Redfin! Bathroom Tips Before Selling
Sep 16 
Written By Mel Kelly

We’re excited to share that Haven Reno KC was recently featured by Redfin in their article “9 Ways to Get Your Bathrooms Open-House Ready.”

Redfin asked home and remodeling professionals what homeowners should prioritize when preparing a bathroom for an open house, including which small improvements make the strongest impression and which updates may not be worth the investment before selling.

We shared a few of the things we notice all the time in bathrooms around Lee’s Summit and the Kansas City area.

And the good news? Most of them don’t require a remodel.

Before Selling, Focus on “Clean and Cared For”

If you’re planning to sell your home soon, a dated bathroom doesn’t necessarily mean you should remodel it.

In fact, we shared with Redfin:

“Even if your bathroom looks a little sad, it’s unlikely you’ll get a return on your investment with a full remodel. Priority wise, you’ll get a much better return with fresh paint on your walls, trim and ideally your ceiling too. If budget allows, an updated light fixture also makes a great investment. Peeling, moldy caulk and stained grout are two small details that can gross out buyers in an instant, but fresh caulk and grout cleaning are such easy, inexpensive fixes, especially compared to a remodel.”

The goal before an open house should usually be to make the bathroom feel clean, bright, maintained and move-in ready, rather than trying to completely transform it.

Here are a few of the smaller updates we recommend.

1. Make Sure Your Light Bulbs Match

This may be one of the easiest bathroom improvements people overlook.

Make sure every bulb in the bathroom matches in both style and color temperature.

If one bulb is warm yellow, another is bright white and another has a bluish cast, the entire bathroom can feel disjointed, even when buyers can’t immediately explain why.

For our bathroom remodeling projects, we typically use 3000K lighting.

It gives bathrooms a nice balance: bright and clean without feeling overly harsh or clinical, but not so warm that everything starts looking yellow.

Lighting affects how buyers see your paint colors, countertops, tile, cabinetry and even how clean the room appears. Before spending money replacing larger finishes, start by making sure the lighting is working in your favor.

2. Freshen Up Your Paint

Fresh paint is one of the most cost-effective ways to make a bathroom feel cared for.

Look beyond just the walls.

Check the:

Walls

Baseboards and trim

Doors

Ceiling

Bathrooms are especially prone to scuffs, moisture staining and dingy ceilings.

If the room needs a refresh, a clean coat of paint can make a surprisingly big difference without requiring a major renovation.

If you need inspiration, we’ve also put together some of our favorite neutral paint colors that work beautifully in homes around the Kansas City area.

3. Replace an Outdated Vanity Light if the Budget Allows

If you have a little more room in the budget, take a look at the vanity light.

Lighting fixtures tend to visually date a bathroom very quickly.

Replacing an older fixture with something clean and current can modernize the entire vanity wall without replacing the vanity, countertop or mirror.

And because lighting has such a major impact on how a space feels, this is one area where a relatively small investment can have an outsized visual effect.

4. Replace Peeling or Moldy Caulk

Nothing screams “there might be a maintenance problem here” quite like peeling, moldy or badly discolored caulk.

Fortunately, this is also one of the least expensive things to fix.

Fresh caulk around the shower, tub and countertop can immediately make a bathroom feel cleaner and better maintained.

The same goes for grout.

If your grout is dark or stained, a good grout cleaning can make existing tile look dramatically better without replacing any of it.

5. Clean the Shower Glass

Glass shower doors show water spots, mineral buildup and soap residue very easily, especially when sunlight or bathroom lighting hits the glass.

If you have glass shower doors, give them some extra attention before listing photos or an open house.

We actually wrote an entire guide on how to keep glass shower doors sparkling clean, including the simple maintenance routine we recommend to our remodeling clients.

6. Make Your Hardware Feel Intentional

Look around the room at your:

Cabinet hardware

Towel bars

Toilet paper holder

Faucets

Shower hardware

Light fixture

Everything does not necessarily have to be identical, but the finishes should look intentional.

If the room has an assortment of bright chrome, brushed nickel, oil-rubbed bronze and gold that accumulated through years of individual repairs, simplifying some of those finishes can help the room feel more cohesive.

You don’t need to replace every plumbing fixture to accomplish this.

Sometimes swapping cabinet hardware or accessories is enough.

Should You Remodel a Bathroom Before Selling?

Usually, we wouldn’t recommend starting a full bathroom remodel solely because you’re preparing to list your home.

If the bathroom functions properly but simply looks dated, smaller cosmetic improvements are often the more practical choice.

But that’s very different from remodeling a bathroom because you plan to stay in the home and want it to work better for your family.

That’s when larger improvements like a new layout, custom cabinetry, better storage, improved lighting, updated tile or a larger shower can make a lot more sense.

For example, take a look at our Lee’s Summit Spa Bathroom Remodel before and after to see how dramatically a dated primary bathroom can change when the goal is creating a space homeowners will actually enjoy living in.

We also completed a green bathroom remodel in Lee’s Summit that shows how color, tile, lighting and thoughtful storage can completely change the feeling of a smaller bathroom.

Read Our Feature on Redfin

Thank you to Amanda Tripp and Redfin for including Haven Reno KC in this article and allowing us to share our perspective.

You can read the full article here:

“9 Ways to Get Your Bathrooms Open-House Ready” on Redfin.

The article was written by Amanda Tripp and originally published by Redfin on September 16, 2026.

If you’re staying in your home and your bathroom isn’t working for you anymore, that’s a different conversation.

At Haven Reno KC, we help homeowners in Lee’s Summit and surrounding communities create bathrooms that are beautiful, functional and comfortable to live with every day.

We can help with everything from layout and cabinetry to tile, countertops, paint colors, lighting and the finishing details that pull the space together.
